chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him about a man who said to three of his slave-girls, 'You are free,' while he had four of them. A man from the people asked him, 'Have you freed your slave-girls?' He said, 'Yes.' He asked, 'Does emancipation become obligatory for all four at the time he grouped them together, or is it only for the three whom he freed?' He said, 'Emancipation becomes obligatory only for whom he freed.'

key_terms.أَجْمَلَهُمْ: He grouped them together / included them collectively
key_terms.عِتْقٌ: Emancipation or freeing of a slave

ai.seo_question: Does declaring 'you are free' to three slaves while owning four make all four free?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of specific designation (*takhassus*) in manumission, ruling that emancipation applies only to those explicitly named or intended by the master's declaration, rather than automatically extending to all slaves present. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise intent (*niyyah*) and linguistic specificity of the master's words, distinguishing it from general group emancipation. It serves as a foundational precedent for understanding conditional or partial manumission in Islamic inheritance and property law.
